title: Interaction fidelity sweep: buttons, tokens, tables, charts on Safari/Firefox/mobile
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Run a platform-wide QA sweep of the design system focusing on interaction fidelity and visual regression for tokens (color/spacing/typography), primary/secondary buttons, responsive table behaviors, and SVG/chart rendering across Safari (desktop + iOS), Firefox (desktop + Android webview), and mobile Chromium variants. Goal is to catalog regressions, assign fixes, and land targeted patches before the ui-kit-2026.03 release. This ticket aggregates findings, triage decisions, and follow-ups. Acceptance criteria: 1) Critical interaction regressions fixed or have tracked ENG tickets. 2) Visual token mismatches documented with reproductions and Figma references. 3) Accessibility touch target and focus ring inconsistencies resolved or scoped out with compensating controls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Pull branch: figma-tokens/2026-02 and deploy storybook build (internal)
2) Use test matrix: desktop Safari 16.5, Safari iOS 16.5, Firefox 112+, Chrome Android 114+, iPhone 12/SE viewport profiles
3) Compare primary/secondary button components in Storybook canvas against Figma token frame 'Buttons / Primary (Default, Hover, Focus, Disabled)'
4) Open tables with long cell content and resize viewport widths to confirm column overflow, horizontal scroll behavior, and sticky header consistency
5) Load charts story (LineChart/StackedBar) with SVG axis labels and pixel-ratio 2, inspect axis tick alignment and canvas vs svg antialiasing
6) Record artifacts (screenshots, video), annotate with expected vs actual token values and collect CSS/DOM snapshots

acceptance_criteria: Critical regressions are either fixed and merged or have eng tickets with estimates and owners
Token mismatches have Figma references and are either reverted or have documented migration steps
Buttons meet touch target and focus visibility requirements on iOS Safari and Firefox mobile webview
Table horizontal overflow behavior is consistent across tested browsers; sticky headers don't overlap content on narrow viewports
Charts render axis labels crisply at DPR=2 and match visual spec; any remaining antialiasing differences are documented with screenshots
notes: Observations: Safari recently changed backdrop-filter rendering which caused semi-transparent button overlays to appear heavier — workaround may require changing overlay alpha or compositing layer hints.
Firefox issue: SVG subpixel ticks shift by 0.5px when CSS transform is present on container; possible fix is to round transforms or render axis on rect-aligned positions.
Temporary plan: ship a canary Storybook with reverted token aliasing for colors used in buttons and charts; run smoke tests, then forward-port the minimal change.
Follow-ups: DES-21358 => token normalization; DES-21359 => typography micro-adjustments; ENG-4821 => runtime button shadow fix with perf regression check.
